result.summary: Plugs Bitcoin Core's hardware-optimized SHA256 compression function into libsecp256k1 contexts. It retires the ECC_Context RAII lifecycle class in favor of thread-safe, on-first-use static contexts for signing and public operations, and replaces uses of secp256k1_context_static across pubkey, MuSig2, and BIP352 code with these accelerated contexts.
result.problem: libsecp256k1 relies on its internal portable SHA256 implementation by default, leaving hardware crypto acceleration (SHA-NI, ARMv8, SSE4) unused during signing and internal hashing. In addition, libsecp256k1's static context cannot accept a custom compression function, and the previous ECC_Context pattern required boilerplate RAII lifecycle management throughout node binaries, tools, benchmarks, and tests.
evidence: Author's benchmarks on ARM64 using arm_shani report a 13% reduction in ECDSASign latency (79.2 µs to 69.3 µs) and a 7% reduction in SchnorrSign latency (39.9 µs to 37.1 µs), with smaller improvements in EllSwiftCreate (-3%) and BIP324_ECDH (-1%).
result.scope_notes: Much of the diff is mechanical boilerplate removal of ECC_Context across binaries, tests, and benchmarks, as well as scripted-diff replacements of secp256k1_context_static.
result.changed_since_previous: Rather than moving ECC_Context management into separate ecc_context and ecc_init files, ECC_Context is completely eliminated; both signing and public contexts are now created lazily on first use.
result.card: Plugs Bitcoin Core's hardware-optimized SHA256 compression routine into libsecp256k1 contexts and removes the ECC_Context RAII class across the codebase in favor of lazily initialized global contexts. Replaces secp256k1_context_static across pubkey, MuSig2, and BIP352 operations so they can leverage hardware acceleration. Benchmarks on ARM64 show a 13% speedup for ECDSA signing and a 7% speedup for Schnorr signing, with minimal impact on signature verification. No dependencies are listed.

risk.why: A flaw in the SHA256 transform hook or context initialization could produce invalid signatures or break signature verification across node and wallet operations.
